what_this_is: The feature flag and pilot allowlist for the FAST_DATA_ONLY_RELEASE lane. The lane may PROVE a sealed market package FAST_DATA_ONLY_RELEASE_ELIGIBLE = YES, but a Regression V2 plan may replace the broad regression with that proof only when FAST_PATH_PRODUCTION_ACTIVATION is ENABLED and the package's market is in pilot_allowlist. Until ATLAS-THROUGHPUT-004/005 integrate the artifact and release lifecycle, both stay closed: the fast path cannot silently replace the production deployment workflow.
persistent_cache_note: ATLAS-THROUGHPUT-004: scripts/pettripfinder/bundle_cache.py proves an unchanged validated market bundle reusable across runs. A cache hit proves artifact identity, never release safety; the production assembler and deployer do not consume the cache until ATLAS-THROUGHPUT-005 integrates it into the release coordinator.
activation_requires: ATLAS-THROUGHPUT-005 release coordinator consuming validation receipts
a founder decision recorded in this file, per market, with the receipt digest it trusts
production_release_consumption_note: PRODUCTION_RELEASE_CONSUMPTION stays DISABLED and is deliberately NOT opened: it governs consuming a cached validated bundle, and Lexington has never been built, so the cache probe was a MISS and the lane built it cold. Opening a flag this launch does not need would widen the blast radius for nothing.

consumed.why_closed: same lifecycle as the coordinator gate: opened for one candidate, consumed by its activation, closed. The redesigned factory itself is NOT disabled -- FAST_PATH_IMPLEMENTED and FAST_PATH_VALIDATED stay YES and the lane remains the normal validation path; what closes is the standing permission to ACTIVATE production without a fresh founder decision.
